problem.statement: Open Food Network Canada reports a map-centering and zoom bug: one mis-geocoded enterprise can shift the map to another continent, making local sellers hard for shoppers to find.

sources.claim: Open issue #14924 describes a real Canadian instance problem and reports a user threatening to leave; maintainer issue text is not independent churn measurement.

candidate_asset.description: Established open-source marketplace linking growers, food hubs and purchasers across a global nonprofit network.
candidate_asset.caveat: Repository activity/popularity measures do not establish user adoption, commercial underconversion or profit.

cross_layer_fit.documented_capability: Open Food Network includes a public /map for producer discovery and a MapCentreCalculator setting map center from enterprise coordinates.
cross_layer_fit.required_mechanism: A robust, locale-aware map should display the intended country's sellers even if one enterprise is geocoded outside the service geography.
cross_layer_fit.unverified_gap: Issue #14924 identifies extreme-coordinate midpoint and hard-coded zoom defects; no patch, review or measured retention impact is demonstrated in this assessment.
cross_layer_fit.limitation: A semantic match is not proof of operational implementation, stakeholder fit or economic value.

buyer.segment: Open Food Foundation engineering team or existing country instance operators (paid contractor fit to confirm)

signals.claim: A published open bug documents current engineering need but not a paid budget for this task.

buyer.limitation: The business willingness-to-pay is not inferred from a research problem or popularity counts.

signals.claim: The foundation publicly advertises applications for paid developer and system administrator contributions; no specific offer or contract has been received.
Maintainer issue names a concrete open engineering problem; it does not promise paid engagement.

unit_economics.limitation: No observed selling price or total delivery cost; no revenue projection.

results.recommended_next_test: Check whether the paid contributor application remains open and propose one bounded deliverable.

underconversion.why: GitHub usage counters and repository feature lists do not establish a monetization gap or economically addressable demand.
alternatives: Existing deployments may already serve buyers
Maintainers may intentionally reject commercial arrangements
Market access or service economics may be the binding constraint
underconversion.next_evidence: Interview operators, determine alternatives/budgets, assess conversion rights, and validate adoption economics.

results.boundary: Research/technical reconnaissance only; no partner contact, contract, code reuse, license clearance or customer validation performed.

problem.statement: Foodsoft's cooperative order-balancing UI can flag false mismatches when article quantities are rounded to three decimals but the summed group-order quantities are not.

sources.claim: Issue #1368 reports an explicit unit rounding discrepancy and a minimal code-location lead; this is software maintainer feedback, not proof of demand for paid consulting.

candidate_asset.description: Nonprofit food cooperative software for product ordering, cooperative accounting and job scheduling.
candidate_asset.caveat: Repository activity/popularity measures do not establish user adoption, commercial underconversion or profit.

cross_layer_fit.documented_capability: Foodsoft supports member group orders and accounting/balancing views with a quantity-difference diagnostic.
cross_layer_fit.required_mechanism: Price and quantity reconciliation must compare values consistently at the same precision without suppressing real order mismatches.
cross_layer_fit.unverified_gap: Issue #1368 identifies a precision mismatch; a safe fix and regression fixture still need to be executed. No contract or local deployment demand is confirmed.
cross_layer_fit.limitation: A semantic match is not proof of operational implementation, stakeholder fit or economic value.

problem.statement: Taiwan's periodic dog-population surveys and research on mark-recapture imply an investigation requirement for repeatable sightings with photographic identity records; this is not a confirmed local agency procurement request.

sources.claim: Population estimation literature describes the importance of identification and repeat observation for free-roaming dog abundance estimation.
Taiwan's 2024 national dog estimate and periodic survey methodology do not establish a continuously tracked local population.

candidate_asset.description: Open-source form/data collection infrastructure for field operations and surveys.
candidate_asset.caveat: Repository activity/popularity measures do not establish user adoption, commercial underconversion or profit.

cross_layer_fit.documented_capability: KoboToolbox provides offline forms and API access to survey records and attachments, potentially allowing dog sighting photos to be collected.
cross_layer_fit.required_mechanism: Repeated dog-specific sightings with location/time/photo provenance, individual reconciliation, and valid population-estimation assumptions.
cross_layer_fit.unverified_gap: A dog-identification model and statistical abundance estimator would remain separate; no end-to-end field proof or Taiwan authority willingness-to-pay has been established.
cross_layer_fit.limitation: A semantic match is not proof of operational implementation, stakeholder fit or economic value.

buyer.segment: Potential animal-control departments, shelters, research organizations and field survey contractors
buyer.limitation: The business willingness-to-pay is not inferred from a research problem or popularity counts.

unit_economics.limitation: No observed selling price or total delivery cost; no revenue projection.

results.recommended_next_test: Run a minimal capability-to-requirement test before proposing deployment.

problem.statement: Surplus-food donors and recipients face coordination, pickup and handling frictions, while published redistribution interventions rarely establish long-term beneficiary outcomes.

sources.claim: A scoping review discusses surplus-food redistribution models and structural limitations, not demonstrated buyer demand for this particular MVP.

candidate_asset.description: A community surplus-food listing, discovery, claim and pickup prototype with published unverified feature claims.
candidate_asset.caveat: Repository activity/popularity measures do not establish user adoption, commercial underconversion or profit.

cross_layer_fit.documented_capability: README claims authentication, listings, geo-discovery, atomic claiming and pickup completion.
cross_layer_fit.required_mechanism: Reliable donor-to-recipient posting, collection and traceability without unsafe food handling or identity/access failures.
cross_layer_fit.unverified_gap: No observed real adoption, business/organization onboarding, operator safety verification, food safety liability assessment or external buyer commitment. Public README mentions MIT despite no detected root license file.
cross_layer_fit.limitation: A semantic match is not proof of operational implementation, stakeholder fit or economic value.

buyer.limitation: The business willingness-to-pay is not inferred from a research problem or popularity counts.

unit_economics.limitation: No observed selling price or total delivery cost; no revenue projection.

results.recommended_next_test: Ask maintainer about license/permission; do not copy, deploy or sell the code yet.
